questions.question: What is the main ingredient of guacamole?
questions.explanation: Guacamole comes from Mexico and is made from mashed avocado.

questions.question: Which grain is the main ingredient of traditional risotto?
questions.explanation: Arborio or carnaroli rice is typically used.

questions.question: Which spice gives curry its yellow colour?
questions.explanation: Turmeric contains the pigment curcumin.

questions.question: Which fruit is the main ingredient of wine?
questions.explanation: Wine is made by fermenting grape juice.

questions.question: Does all the alcohol cook off when a dish is briefly simmered with wine?
questions.explanation: Alcohol evaporates gradually; short cooking leaves much of it in the dish.
questions.misconception: Many people think all the alcohol cooks off when a dish is simmered with wine.

questions.question: Does searing meat 'seal in the juices'?
choices: No, it browns the surface but does not seal moisture
Yes, it forms a waterproof crust
questions.explanation: Seared meat can lose as much moisture as unseared meat; the crust adds flavour, not a seal.
questions.misconception: Many people think searing meat seals in its juices.

questions.question: At what temperature in Celsius does water boil at sea level?
questions.explanation: Water boils at 100 °C (212 °F) at standard pressure.

questions.question: Which leavener already contains an acid, so it can raise a batter by itself?
questions.explanation: Baking powder is baking soda plus a dry acid; baking soda needs an acid in the recipe.
questions.misconception: Many people think baking soda and baking powder are the same thing.

questions.question: Which country is the origin of sushi as most people know it?
questions.explanation: Modern nigiri sushi developed in Edo (Tokyo) in the 1800s.

questions.question: Which Italian dish is made with layers of pasta, meat sauce and béchamel?
questions.explanation: Lasagna is baked in the oven in layers.

questions.question: Which cheese is traditionally used on a Margherita pizza?
questions.explanation: Margherita has tomato, mozzarella and basil, echoing Italy's flag.

questions.question: What is the name of the French dish of thin pancakes?
questions.explanation: Crêpes originate in Brittany.

questions.question: Which fungus is a luxury ingredient found by trained pigs or dogs?
questions.explanation: Truffles grow underground near tree roots.

questions.question: What is the main ingredient of hummus?
questions.explanation: Hummus also contains tahini, lemon and garlic.

questions.question: Which herb is the main ingredient of pesto?
questions.explanation: Pesto genovese uses basil, pine nuts, Parmesan, garlic and olive oil.

questions.question: Which dairy product is made by churning cream?
questions.explanation: Churning separates butterfat from buttermilk.

questions.question: What is 'mise en place' in cooking?
choices: Having ingredients prepared and in place before cooking
questions.explanation: It is French for 'putting in place'.

questions.question: What does 'al dente' mean when cooking pasta?
questions.explanation: Italian for 'to the tooth'.

questions.question: Which sauce is made from egg yolks, butter and lemon juice?
questions.explanation: Hollandaise is one of the five French mother sauces.

questions.question: Which type of pastry is used to make a classic croissant?
questions.explanation: Layers of butter are folded into yeasted dough.

questions.question: What is the Japanese dish of seasoned vinegar rice with raw fish called?
questions.explanation: Sashimi is sliced raw fish served without rice.

questions.question: Which country is paella from?
questions.explanation: Paella originated in Valencia.

questions.question: Which fermented Korean side dish is made from cabbage and chilli?
questions.explanation: Kimchi is a staple of Korean cuisine.

questions.question: Which country is famous for the dish 'pad thai'?
questions.explanation: Pad thai is a stir-fried noodle dish.

questions.question: Which ingredient gives a classic Caesar dressing its creamy base, alongside anchovy, garlic and oil?
questions.explanation: Classic Caesar dressing has egg yolk, anchovy, garlic, lemon and oil.

questions.question: What is the Italian word for 'coffee with milk foam' served in the morning?
questions.explanation: Cappuccino is espresso with steamed milk and foam.

questions.question: Which spice is the most expensive by weight, harvested from crocus flowers?
questions.explanation: Each flower yields only three stigmas.

questions.question: Which flour is used for traditional Neapolitan pizza?
questions.explanation: Finely milled '00' flour is common in Italy.

questions.question: Which country does the cheese Gruyère come from?
questions.explanation: Gruyère is named after the town of Gruyères.

questions.question: Which type of rice is used for sushi?
questions.explanation: Short-grain rice is sticky when cooked.

questions.question: What chemical reaction browns bread crust and seared steak?
questions.explanation: The Maillard reaction involves amino acids and sugars.

questions.question: Which living ingredient makes traditional bread dough rise?
questions.explanation: Yeast ferments sugars producing carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Which are the five French 'mother sauces'?
questions.explanation: Auguste Escoffier codified them in the early 1900s.

questions.question: Which Mexican sauce is made with chilies, chocolate and spices?
questions.explanation: Mole poblano is the best-known version.

questions.question: Which Michelin rating is the highest?
questions.explanation: Three stars mean 'exceptional cuisine, worth a special journey'.

questions.question: What is the Japanese stock made from kelp and bonito flakes?
questions.explanation: Dashi is the base of miso soup.

questions.question: Which Indian bread is cooked in a tandoor?
questions.explanation: A tandoor is a clay oven.

questions.question: Which chef is credited with codifying modern French cuisine and the brigade system?
questions.explanation: Escoffier organised kitchens into brigades.

questions.question: What is 'umami'?
questions.explanation: Umami was identified by Kikunae Ikeda in 1908.

questions.question: Which compound makes chilli peppers hot?
questions.explanation: The Scoville scale measures chilli heat.

questions.question: What temperature in Celsius is a typical safe internal temperature for cooked chicken?
questions.explanation: Food safety agencies recommend 165 °F / 74 °C.

questions.question: Which Spanish cold tomato soup is served in summer?
questions.explanation: Gazpacho comes from Andalusia.
